title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page of the 1976 PD de Rham notes. It is a typed page, p.119 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 I, Grothendieck's "Modèles de Néron et monodromie" (LNM 288, 1972). It was evidently reused as scrap paper: the neighbouring handwritten pages on divided-power de Rham cochain algebras are presumably on the versos of such sheets.

Mathematical content, in modern terms. Let S be a henselian trait with fraction field K, and A_K an abelian variety with semistable reduction. The ℓ-adic Tate module T_ℓ(A_K) carries the three-step monodromy filtration
  T_ℓ ⊃ T_ℓ^f (fixed part) ⊃ T_ℓ^t (toric part) ⊃ 0.
This filtration is used as the 'extension panachée' (mixed extension, in the sense of SGA 7 Exp. IX §9.3–9.5) X_η of E_η by F_η, with graded pieces Q, R, P.
- The identification X^1 ≅ F_η (as extensions of R by P) is immediate.
- The identification of X/X^2 with the extension of Q by R, which is dual to F'_η for the dual abelian variety, follows from the orthogonality theorem 5.2. That theorem says T^t and T'^f are exact orthogonals under the Weil pairing.
- The general construction 9.5.6 then attaches a pairing to the mixed extension. Here Q* = M'_ℓ, so this is the monodromy pairing (9.1.2) between the character groups of the toric parts of the Néron models of A and A'. By 9.5.8 it agrees with the earlier definition in 9.2.
- By 5.8, and assuming Tate's theorem on p-divisible groups (known when char K = 0), the pairing depends only on the ℓ-pro-Barsotti–Tate group T_ℓ(A_K) over S. The reason is that its filtration and the extensions E, F prolonging X^1 and X/X^2 are canonically determined by it. This matters when ℓ equals the residue characteristic.

Remark 9.7 begins the extension to potentially semistable reduction. One takes a finite Galois extension K'/K over which A acquires semistable reduction and defines the monodromy pairing by Galois descent from A_{K'}.
errors: As transcribed, the second isomorphism reads 'X_η/X_η^2 ≃ F_η = D(F'_η)'. Logically, X/X^2 is the extension of Q by R, which is E_η, so it should read 'E_η = D(F'_η)'. This is either a typo in the typescript or a misreading; check against the printed SGA 7.
